A scholar, astronomer and inventor of the Eastern Han dynasty, who worked at the court in Luoyang. He served as chief astronomer and was also a well known poet.

His best known inventions:

  • An armillary sphere, a model of the heavens with rings, turned by water so that it kept time with the stars.
  • A seismoscope built in 132: a bronze jar with eight dragons around it. When the ground shook, a ball fell from a dragon's mouth into a toad below, showing the direction of the quake. The record says it once detected an earthquake far to the west that no one in the capital had felt.

He also wrote that the Moon shines by reflected sunlight, mapped thousands of stars and worked on the value of pi. Later histories treat him as the model of the learned official. Like Ptolemy, his near contemporary in Alexandria, he joined careful observation with geometry.
sum: A scholar, astronomer and inventor of the Eastern Han dynasty, who worked at the court in Luoyang. He served as chief astronomer and was also a well known poet.
